SUMMARY: Sign-out failure message is false: the client signs you out locally anyway
USER_STORY: As a user whose sign-out request failed, I want to be told the truth, so I know whether my session is still open.
DESCRIPTION: src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx `signOut` (assumes a failed `supabase.auth.signOut()` leaves the session; supabase-js 2.116.0 clears it locally regardless). The `signout` copy is in src/lib/authErrors.ts. Found by LED-124 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-live-sweep-shell-search-system.md), from LED-11. Observed: With /auth/v1/logout blocked, clicking Sign out: within 100 ms sb-127-auth-token is removed and the app is on /login, showing 'Sign-out failed. You're still signed in on this device.' AuthContext.signOut assumes a failed signOut() leaves the session (comment: 'A failed sign-out leaves the user signed in'); @supabase/supabase-js 2.116.0 clears the local session regardless, so the user is signed out locally with a server session still valid, and the copy is wrong. shots/124-auth-signout-blocked.png. Local cache and queue are left in place (the clear step is skipped). Suggested fix: Decide the behaviour: (1) accept the local sign-out and say "Signed out here, but we could not reach the server; your session may stay open elsewhere until it expires", and still clear the local cache and queue on this device; or (2) call `signOut({ scope: "local" })` deliberately and revoke server-side on next load. Update the copy and the comment.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) With `/auth/v1/logout` blocked, Sign out lands on /login with a message that matches what happened; (b) the message does not say "still signed in" when the token is gone; (c) local cache, queue and pending receipts are cleared or the user is told they were kept and why; (d) unit test for the error mapping; (e) LED-11 acceptance still holds.
